executionScopes.title: Personality library: reusable character profiles (name + description + LLM + TTS voice) assignable to calendar events / playground; renders the per-session bot name in history
executionScopes.description:
## Why this exists

Today the bots character lives in two implicit places: a single system prompt buried in the global settings, plus whichever LLM + TTS providers happen to be active. Switching from "Johnny — neutral assistant" to "a different character" today means editing that prompt, swapping the active LLM, and swapping the active TTS — for every session, by hand, with no way to keep the old setup around.

The product idea is to lift "the character" into a first-class object: a **personality**. Each personality is a name + a plain-text description (traits, communication style, anything else the operator writes) plus the LLM provider/model and TTS provider/voice that personality should use. Once created, personalities are assignable on the two surfaces the bot actually runs from today — calendar events (one per meeting) and the playground page — and revertible without re-typing anything.

> **Surface audit.** Existing frontend routes (verified): `calendar/`, `history/`, `playground/`, `providers/`, `sessions/`, `settings/`, `templates/`. There is NO standalone "chat" route — the playground is the chat-style live surface and history is the read-only transcript view. Both display the bot under the hardcoded name "Johnny" (`frontend/src/routes/history/[id]/+page.svelte:217,234`). Personalities replace that hardcoding by snapshotting the personality's display name onto the session at start and rendering history rows / titles from the snapshot instead of the constant.

The operator can have a library: "Johnny" (the default), "Friendly Customer Support", "Skeptical Code Reviewer", "Calm Therapist". Each carries its own voice and its own model. Switching between them is a one-click assignment, not a config rewrite.

## What lives ON a personality vs OFF it

| On the personality | Off the personality (stays global) | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Display name | — | The name the operator picks the personality by. |
| Description (free text) | — | Goes into the system prompt at session start. Where the character lives. |
| LLM provider + model | — | Different models have noticeably different voice / pacing / tone. The operator explicitly called this out. |
| TTS provider + voice | — | The single biggest carrier of perceived character. |
| Default bot mode (listen / suggest / approval / autonomous) — OPTIONAL | If the personality leaves it blank, falls back to the meeting / playground default. | Some characters only make sense in certain modes (an "autonomous skeptic" is a different bot from a "suggest-only skeptic"). |
| — | STT provider | STT does not meaningfully affect perceived character; keeping it global avoids re-configuring the STT side every time the operator wants a different voice on the same recording pipeline. |

## How it composes with the existing system

- Personalities are **NOT** template substitutes. A template is a conversation pattern (intro / interview / standup); a personality is *who* is running it. The two compose: a meeting picks a template AND a personality.
- At session start, the providers loader (`backend/app/providers/loader.py:load_active_providers`) reads the chosen personality FIRST and uses its LLM + TTS overrides; falls back to the global active providers when the personality leaves a slot blank.
- The existing global "Johnny" system prompt + the currently-active LLM + the currently-active TTS get migrated into a built-in personality called "Johnny", marked as the default. Nothing changes for an operator who never touches the personalities page; the default keeps working.

## Sub-tasks (filed as children below)

1. **Design + PRD** — read the current provider-loader + system-prompt flow end to end, propose the personality data model, decide override rules (what fallback when the personality references an unconfigured provider), decide UI placement. Blocks everything else.
2. **Backend: data model + CRUD API + Johnny-default migration** — new `personalities` table, REST endpoints (list / create / clone / get / update / delete / set-default), Alembic migration that lifts the current globals into a built-in "Johnny" personality without data loss.
3. **Backend: personality-driven provider resolution at session start** — `load_active_providers` reads the chosen personality, swaps LLM + TTS to the personality-specified rows, falls back loudly (logged + surfaced in the session UI) when the personality references a provider the operator deleted or deactivated.
4. **Frontend: personality library management page** — list / create-from-scratch / clone / edit / delete / set-as-default. New route `/personalities`. Form fields: name, description (textarea), LLM picker, TTS picker (uses the unified voice component from Johnny-1ge.8), optional bot-mode override.
5. **Frontend: personality picker integrated into calendar events + playground + history bot-name rendering** — the two surfaces that pick a personality at session start (calendar event detail, playground) gain a dropdown; the history view stops rendering the hardcoded `'Johnny'` constant and reads the per-session bot name from the snapshot taken at session start. Active-session card surfaces the personality name too.
6. **End-to-end test matrix** — backend unit + integration tests for every CRUD endpoint, every override-resolution branch, every fallback path. Frontend browser tests via chrome-devtools MCP that drive: create a personality, assign it to a calendar event, start a session, verify the right LLM + TTS were loaded, verify the system prompt contains the personality description. Reproducible in CI without a live Meet.

## Acceptance for the epic

- A new operator with no personalities defined sees nothing change — the Johnny default behaves exactly like the current global setup.
- An operator can create a second personality, assign it to a calendar event, start that meeting, and the bot uses the personality-specified LLM + TTS, with the description in the system prompt.
- History rows for that session render the personality's name where today they render the hardcoded `'Johnny'`. Pre-personality sessions keep showing "Johnny" because that is what was true at the time.
- The personality the bot is currently using is surfaced in the active-session UI (so the operator can tell at a glance which character is in the meeting).
- Every sub-task lands with its own tests; the test matrix in `.7` runs in CI on every PR.
- README has a new "Personalities" section explaining the concept in 4-5 sentences and pointing at `/personalities`.

## Non-goals

- Mid-session personality swap. Personality is picked at session start and held for the rest of the session.
- Personality-conditioned templates / personality-conditioned routing. The personality is consumed by the LLM (as system prompt) and the TTS (as voice). Anything that needs the router to *behave differently* per personality belongs in the Johnny-etu pipeline epic, not here.
- Multi-personality conversations (Johnny + a second character in the same meeting). Single-personality-per-session is the v1 scope.
- Cloud personalities marketplace, sharing, presets. Local-only library; one operator owns their personalities the same way they own their providers.

## Cross-links

- **Johnny-1ge.8** (unified voice picker UX) — HARD DEPENDENCY for sub-task .4 (the TTS slot inside the personality form uses that component).
- **Johnny-etu** epic (pipeline + decision-making revision) — the per-session reasoning timeline (Johnny-ckz.28.4) should display which personality is active so an operator reading the timeline knows whose voice they expect.
- **Johnny-etu.1 / .etu.2** (pipeline docs) — both get a short subsection on how personalities feed into the pipeline at session start.
- **Johnny-fe** (frontend overhaul epic) — the new `/personalities` page must be designed in the shadcn-svelte system landing under that epic.
- **Johnny-ckz** epic — every closed sub-task that touched "system prompt" or "active provider selection" (Johnny-vgl, Johnny-7qp, Johnny-ckz.2 autonomous mode, Johnny-d3e provider seed) is context the design agent should re-read.

## Reference

- Current provider loader: `backend/app/providers/loader.py:load_active_providers`.
- Where the system prompt lives today: search `backend/app/services/` for prompt assembly; specifically the place that interpolates the global Johnny prompt into the per-turn LLM call.
- Templates table (do not confuse with personalities): `backend/app/db/models.py`.
